title: Fantasy Player News
description: Breaking Fantasy Football player news along with the impact for fantasy managers

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Odell Beckham Jr. to be elevated by Vikings Sunday
items.desc: The Vikings will elevate WR Odell Beckham Jr. from their practice squad for Sunday's game against the Saints.
items.impact: Beckham signed with Minnesota earlier this week. He will remain off the fantasy radar.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Darius Slayton (knee) ruled out Sunday
items.desc: Darius Slayton has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Steelers.
items.impact: Slayton had been listed as questionable. His absence won't impact the Colts offense for fantasy managers.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Marvin Harrison Jr: Cardinals finalizing trade
items.desc: The Cardinals are finalizing a deal to trade WR Marvin Harrison Jr.
items.impact: The Cardinals informed Harrison this morning that he will be inactive for Sunday's game against the Lions as the details of the trade are finalized. It remains unclear as of now where he will be traded.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Justin Jefferson (ankle) plans to play Sunday, to see how he feels Saturday
items.desc: ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reports that Justin Jefferson plans to play in Week 5 against the Saints, but the team "has to see how he feels on Saturday."
items.impact: We should know by the end of Saturday if Jefferson will be good to go on Sunday. He will be a WR1 play if he is good to go.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Jayden Daniels (elbow) still not '100 percent' healthy
items.desc: NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reports that Jayden Daniels is not "100 percent" healthy yet.
items.impact: Daniels is still slated to play on Sunday against the Giants, but re-injury risk is a bit of a concern.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Tyler Guyton (back) not dealing with serious injury
items.desc: Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said LT Tyler Guyton's back injury is not considered serious.
items.impact: Guyton left Thursday's game late. He is day-to-day heading into next week.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Nick Bosa (knee/calf) to likely return in Week 6
items.desc: Nick Bosa told reporters it is "pretty darn likely" he plays in Week 6 against the Commanders.
items.impact: Bosa will miss his third straight game on Sunday. He should be back next week.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Zach Charbonnet (knee) uncertain for Week 6
items.desc: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Seattle's Week 6 Thursday Night Football game against the Broncos makes Zach Charbonnet's ramp-up "tricky."
items.impact: Charbonnet has been limited since returning to practice, but a short week in Week 6 makes a return then tricky. It sounds like Week 7 against the Chiefs is more likely when he returns.

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.title: Lamar Jackson (ankle) uncertain for Week 6
items.desc: The Ravens reportedly "do not know" whether Lamar Jackson will play in Week 6 against the Browns.
items.impact: Jackson remains week-to-week after he was ruled out for this Sunday. Tyler Huntley could be seeing more than one start.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Tampa Bay Buccaneers D/ST contain Cowboys in win
items.desc: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers D/ST racked up two interceptions and a fumble recovery in the Buccaneers' 24-16 win over the Cowboys on Thursday.
items.impact: The Bucs' defense was pliable on the Cowboys' first drive of the game, but stiffened significantly after that. They did give up a touchdown in the fourth quarter, but managed to make a crucial interception when Dallas was attempting to force overtime. It was a much better showing than we previously had seen from Tampa's defense, but don't call it a comeback just yet.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Chase McLaughlin has solid night in win
items.desc: Chase McLaughlin hit all three of his PATs and his lone field goal attempt in the Bucs' 24-16 win over the Cowboys on Thursday.
items.impact: McLaughlin bounced back from a down week against the Packers, but the offense was also able to move the ball much more effectively against the hapless Dallas defense, giving McLaughlin more chances than he had previously. He's been perfect on the season so far, going 10-for-10 on Field Goals and 10-for-10 on PATs. He should continue to be a solid kicker for those in need.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Dallas Cowboys D/ST run over Thursday night
items.desc: The Dallas Cowboys D/ST managed a single sack on Thursday in the team's 24-16 loss to Tampa Bay. No other meaningful stats were recorded.
items.impact: This is the state of the Dallas defense, allowing a rookie QB in his second start to lead multiple scoring drives and go up by as many as 14 points, while also getting just one sack and no turnovers. It's been a bad showing by the Dallas defense that began the year showing promise of improvement thanks to offseason additions and draft picks. But it appears another long road is ahead for the team this season, which will have to be carried by its offense.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Brandon Aubrey kick for four points in loss
items.desc: Brandon Aubrey hit his only PAT and field goal attempts in the Cowboys' 24-16 loss to the Bucs on Thursday.
items.impact: Aubrey was hindered by a Dallas offense that sputtered badly after their first drive, failing to do much more in the first half before a field goal. After that, the team was in catch-up mode, and Aubrey didn't see the field again. Better days will come for the star kicker.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Jake Ferguson has critical drop in loss to Bucs
items.desc: Jake Ferguson caught three of six targets for 19 yards in the Cowboys' 24-16 loss to Tampa Bay on Thursday.
items.impact: Ferguson had a critical drop on the Cowboys' final drive as they were trying to tie the game, failing to catch a pass and instead bobbling it straight up and into the arms of LB Alex Anzalone. It was a tough night for the veteran, but better days will come.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Pat Bryant (ankle) placed on injured reserve
items.desc: Pat Bryant (ankle) is being placed on injured reserve and will be out for the next four weeks at least.
items.impact: Bryant recently suffered an ankle injury, and it is serious enough that the team is placing him on short-term injured reserve. That means that he will be sidelined for the next four weeks at least, but it sounds like he's expected to make his return sometime not too long after that. Troy Franklin and Courtland Sutton are both likely to see more work for the Broncos for the foreseeable future in his absence.
